In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah al-Haqqah.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The Inevitable Reality﴾ ﴿What is the Inevitable Reality?﴾.

Al-Haqqah (the Inevitable Reality): it is among the names of the Resurrection (al-qiyamah). After it comes ﴿Thamud and 'Ad denied the Striking Calamity﴾ [al-Haqqah: 4]. It is also among the names of the Resurrection, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And what will make you know what the Striking Calamity is? [It is] the Day when mankind will be like scattered moths﴾ [al-Qari'ah: 3-4].

It was named al-Haqqah because in it the promise of Allah regarding resurrection (al-ba'th) and recompense (al-jaza') becomes true (yahiqqu). It was named al-Qari'ah because it strikes the hearts with its terror: ﴿And you see people as drunken, but they are not drunken﴾ [al-Hajj: 2].

Likewise it is called al-Waqi'ah: ﴿There is no denying its occurrence﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 1-2].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 69, verse 4:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Thamud and 'Ad denied the Striking Calamity﴾ ﴿As for Thamud, they were destroyed by the overwhelming blast﴾

Al-Ṭāghiyah is a form on the pattern of fā'ilah from al-ṭughyān (transgression), which is going beyond the limit in an unrestricted sense, as in His saying: ﴿Indeed, when the water overflowed﴾ [al-Ḥāqqah: 11].

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, man transgresses﴾ [al-'Alaq: 6].

The meaning of al-ṭughyān here has been disputed. Some people said: al-ṭāghiyah is the one who hamstrung the she-camel, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Thamud denied through their transgression when the most wretched of them rose up﴾ [al-Shams: 11-12]. In that case the bā' is causal, meaning: because of their transgressor (al-ṭāghiyah, i.e. the one who hamstrung the camel). It was also said: al-ṭāghiyah is the mighty shout that destroyed them, as evidenced by His saying: ﴿Indeed, We sent upon them a single shout, and they became like the crushed straw of one who builds a pen﴾ [al-Qamar: 31]. In that case the bā' is instrumental, as in your saying: "I wrote with the pen," and "I cut with the knife."

What the Qur'an supports is the second meaning, by His saying: ﴿And in Thamud, when it was said to them, "Enjoy yourselves for a time." Yet they insolently defied the command of their Lord, so the thunderbolt seized them while they were watching﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 43-44]. It was also said: there is no barrier to intending both meanings, because they are mutually implicated, the relation of the caused to its cause, since the first is the cause of the second, as they were a distant people. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿so they insolently defied the command of their Lord, and the thunderbolt seized them﴾ points to this.

So al-'utuw (insolence) is transgression in action, and al-ṣā'iqah (the thunderbolt) is the mighty shout, and He has linked them together with the fā' (so).

The author, al-Shaykh (may God's mercy be upon him and upon us), has already explained this when discussing God's words in Surah Fussilat: ﴿So We sent upon them a furious wind during days of ill omen﴾ [Fussilat: 16], which was mentioned in Fussilat. This detailed account of how 'Ad and Thamud were destroyed clarifies what was stated in summary in Surah al-Fajr, in God's words: ﴿So your Lord poured upon them a scourge of punishment﴾ [al-Fajr: 13].

The verse: "And Pharaoh and those before him, and the overturned cities (al-Mu'tafikat), came with the sin (al-Khati'ah)."

Al-Mu'tafikat: al-Munqalibat (the overturned ones), and they are the towns of the people of Lut.

The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him and on us, had already explained this in detail at His words in (Hud): ﴿So when Our command came, We made its highest part its lowest﴾ [Hud: 82], and in (al-Najm) at His words: ﴿And the overturned city He hurled down﴾ [al-Najm: 53].

Note: Here Allah stated that Pharaoh and those before him, and the overturned cities, came with the sin (al-Khati'ah), which is ﴿they disobeyed the Messenger of their Lord﴾ [al-Haqqah: 10]. Likewise, 'Ad and Thamud denied the Striking Calamity (al-Qari'ah). All of them shared in the sin, which is disobedience to the Messenger: ﴿Pharaoh disobeyed the Messenger﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 16]. However, He seized them with a severe seizure.

He varied the manner of their seizure: He drowned Pharaoh and the people of Nuh, seized Thamud with the Cry, 'Ad with a wind, and the people of Lut by overturning their towns, just as He seized the army of Abraha with birds in flocks (ṭayran ababil). So, is there a correspondence between each nation and its punishment, or is it for variety in punishment, to show His power and His exemplary chastisement of those who disobey the messengers of Allah?

The fact is that every kind of punishment is a sign of power and a chastisement of those upon whom it fell. But the specification of each nation with what befell it raises a question, and perhaps among what the Qur'an indicates, in a light allusion, is (p-٢٥٩) what follows.

As for Pharaoh, he used to say: ﴿Does not the kingdom of Egypt belong to me, and these rivers flow beneath me?﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 51]. Since he boasted with them, Allah made his destruction in them, that is, in their kind (jinsiha).

As for the people of Nuh, when he despaired of them after a thousand years less fifty years, and they began to beget none but a wicked disbeliever, it became necessary to purify the earth of them, and nothing suits that but the Flood.

As for Thamud, they were seized by the transgressing Cry, because they called to their companion, so he took it upon himself and hamstrung (the she-camel). Since their calling to their companion was the cause of the hamstringing of the she-camel, their destruction was by the transgressing Cry.

As for 'Ad, it was for their transgression through their strength, as Allah said of them: ﴿Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with 'Ad, Iram of the pillars, the like of which had not been created in the lands?﴾ [al-Fajr: 6-8]. Whether the "pillars" (imad) refers to the pillars of their houses and palaces, it is a metaphor for the length of their bodies, the abundance of their wealth, and the abundance of strength they possessed. So they were seized by the wind, which is the most gentle and subtle of things, from which they had not expected any harm or severity.

Likewise the army of Abraha: when he came proud of his number and equipment, and brought with him the elephant, the strongest of animals, Allah sent against him the weakest of creatures, the birds: ﴿And He sent against them birds in flocks, striking them with stones of baked clay﴾ [al-Fil: 3-4].

As for the people of Lut, because they reversed the natural order by approaching males instead of females, the recompense was of the same kind as the deed: Allah overturned their towns upon them. And knowledge is with Allah, the Exalted.

There is no doubt that in all of this there is a warning (takhwif) to Quraysh.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the earth and the mountains will be lifted and crushed with a single blow﴾

Its explanation has already been given by the Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, in Surah (al-Kahf), at His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the Day We set the mountains in motion﴾ [al-Kahf: 47].

Allah's statement: ﴿On that Day you will be exposed; not a secret of yours will be concealed﴾.

Its explanation has already been given by the Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, at His statement: ﴿and they will find what they did present [before them]﴾ [al-Kahf: 49].

(p-260) His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then as for him who is given his record in his right hand﴾

The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, has already set out the matter of the taking of books and its reality, at His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the Book will be placed [before them]﴾ [al-Kahf: 49], in Surat al-Kahf.

He likewise discussed it in his book Daf' Iham al-Idtirab (Removing the Illusion of Contradiction), and explained the third category, "from behind their backs." In this there is a detailing concerning the Book, the writing, the recording of deeds, and their being given, with clear and explicit texts, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the Book will be placed, and you will see the criminals fearful of what is in it﴾ [al-Kahf: 49].

And their explicit saying: ﴿Woe to us! What is this Book that leaves nothing small or great but has enumerated it?﴾ [al-Kahf: 49].

And His saying: ﴿Not a word does he utter but that with him is an observer, ready﴾ [Qaf: 18].

And His saying: ﴿Read your record; sufficient is your soul against you this Day as a reckoner﴾ [al-Isra': 14]. It is a written book, published on the Day of Resurrection, which each person reads for himself. This refutes the view of those who make the taking of the book in the right hand or the left a metaphor for good fortune and misfortune. In reality this is nothing but a consequence of a corrupt interpretation, without any evidence for it, and what the usulis (scholars of legal theory) call "play" (la'ib). We ask Allah for safety and well-being.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 69, verse 20:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, I was certain that I would encounter my account.﴾

Ẓann (supposition, conjecture) is an intermediate state between doubt (shakk) and knowledge (ʿilm), and it may sometimes carry the meaning of knowledge when indicators (qarāʾin) are present. Its explanation was already given by the Shaykh (i.e., the author) at His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the criminals will see the Fire and will know that they are going to fall therein﴾ [al-Kahf: 53]; that is, they knew, as indicated by His saying: ﴿and they will not find from it any escape﴾ [al-Kahf: 53]. Here it carries the meaning of knowledge, because ʿaqāʾid (matters of creed) do not admit of ẓann, and certainty (jazm) and knowledge are necessary in them.

The Qur'an has indicated that ẓann may carry the meaning of knowledge, by the implication (mafhūm) of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, some suppositions are sin﴾ [al-Ḥujurāt: 12]. Its implication is that some of it is not sin, and so it is true. Likewise His saying, exalted is He: ﴿those who are certain that they will meet their Lord﴾ [al-Baqarah: 46].

⁕ ⁕ ⁕

The author said in (Daf' Iyhām al-Iḍṭirāb ʿan Āyāt al-Kitāb):

(p. 421) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah al-Ḥāqqah

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, I was certain that I would encounter my account.﴾

The difficulty between this and the verses indicating that ẓann does not suffice, such as His saying: ﴿Indeed, suppositions avail not against the truth at all﴾ [Yūnus: 36], was already resolved in the discussion of His saying: ﴿those who are certain that they will meet their Lord﴾ [al-Baqarah: 46] in Surah al-Baqarah.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿What my wealth has not availed me.﴾

Regarding "mā" it has been said that it is interrogative, meaning "what has my wealth availed me?", and the answer is: nothing. It has also been said that it is negative, meaning that my wealth did not avail me anything on this Day. The second meaning is supported by His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿The Day when neither wealth nor children will benefit﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 88].

And His saying: ﴿His wealth did not avail him, nor what he earned﴾ [Al-Masad: 2].

The Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, has already discussed this in Surat al-Kahf at His saying: ﴿And if I am returned to my Lord...﴾ [Al-Kahf: 36].

And in Surat az-Zukhruf at His saying: ﴿And were it not that mankind would be one community, We would have made...﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 36], the verse.

The Exalted said: ﴿Gone from me is my authority.﴾

That is, there is no authority, no rank, and no power for anyone on that Day, as in His saying: ﴿And they will be presented before your Lord in rows, [and He will say], "You have come to Us just as We created you the first time"﴾ [al-Kahf: 48], barefoot, naked.

And His saying: ﴿And you have certainly come to Us alone, just as We created you the first time, and you have left behind what We bestowed upon you⁠ ⁠behind your backs﴾ [al-An'am: 94].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 69, verse 33:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, he did not believe in Allah, the Mighty﴾ ﴿And did not encourage the feeding of the needy﴾

In it, the not encouraging of feeding the needy is coordinated with not believing in Allah, the Mighty, which indicates that the disbeliever is punished for the branches (of the religion) (furu').

The discussion of this issue has already been presented by the Shaykh (may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him) at the beginning of Surah Fussilat, at His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And woe to the polytheists who do not give zakat﴾ [Fussilat: 6-7]. I had heard from him (may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him) his saying: Just as faith increases through obedience, and the believer is rewarded for his faith and for his obedience, likewise disbelief increases through sins, and the disbeliever is requited for his disbelief and for his disobedience, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those who disbelieve and bar from the way of Allah – We will increase them in punishment upon punishment because of what they used to corrupt﴾ [An-Nahl: 88].

So there is a punishment for disbelief and a punishment for corruption. And among what indicates the increase of disbelief is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve after their belief and then increase in disbelief – their repentance will never be accepted﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 90]. The discussion of the increase of punishment was already presented by the Shaykh (may Allah have mercy on him) at the verse of Surah An-Nahl.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 69, verse 36:

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And no food except from ghislin﴾.

The apparent meaning of this restriction is that the people of the Fire have no food except ghislin (a dripping of pus and filth from the people of the Fire), according to the most correct of the interpretations, because it is on the pattern of fi'lin derived from ghasl (washing), since the pus is as if it were the washing-water of the sores of the people of the Fire. May Allah protect us and the Muslims from it.

Another verse has come indicating that their food is restricted to other than ghislin, namely His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They have no food except from dari'[Al-Ghashiyah: 6]﴾, which is dried shibriq (a thorny plant) according to the most correct of the interpretations. What supports this is the saying of Abu Dhu'ayb:

"He grazed on the lush shibriq until it withered and became dari', and the camel-ticks departed from it."

The scholars have many answers to this; the best of them in my view are two:

The first: that punishment has varieties, and the tormented are of various classes. Among them are those whose only food is from ghislin, and among them are those whose only food is from dari', and among them are those whose only food is zaqqum. What supports this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It has seven gates; for each gate there is a portion apportioned﴾ [Al-Hijr: 44].

The second: that the meaning in all the verses is that they have no food at all, because dari' does not truly fall under the name of food, and beasts do not eat it, so much less do human beings. Likewise ghislin is not from food; so whoever's food is dari' has no food, and whoever's food is ghislin likewise. From this is their saying: "So-and-so has no shade except the sun, and no animal except the animal of Thawban," meaning lice; and what they intend is that he has no shade at all and no animal at all. In light of this there is no difficulty, and Allah knows best.

The saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, it is the word of a noble messenger﴾

Attributing the speech to "the noble Messenger" is in the sense of conveying it, as what follows it confirms, namely His saying ﴿a revelation from the Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Haqqah: 43]. The word "messenger" may refer to the Prophet ﷺ or to Jibril (Gabriel). Regarding Jibril, Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, it is the word of a noble messenger, [who is] possessed of power, with esteem near the Owner of the Throne, obeyed and trustworthy﴾ [at-Takwir: 19–21].

Here, the intended meaning is the Messenger ﷺ, by the indication of His saying, ﴿nor is it the word of a poet﴾ [al-Haqqah: 41] and what is joined to it, because the one accused of that was the Messenger Muhammad ﷺ, and He negated that from him. Thus, in all of this there is an affirmation of the noble attribute for the transmission of the Qur'an: from Muhammad, from Jibril, from Allah. He has alluded to this in the first verse in His saying: ﴿obeyed and trustworthy﴾, and ﴿your companion is not insane﴾ [at-Takwir: 21–22].

So He affirmed soundness and justice for the messengers of Allah in conveying the speech of Allah. In this there is a refutation of what the Quraysh accused the Messenger ﷺ of. And in it also is a refutation of the Rafidah (Rafidites) and their claim of alteration or deficiency in the Qur'an.

**The commentator's words on the verse:** ﴿And if he had fabricated against Us some sayings﴾

The Shaykh, may God's mercy be upon us and upon him, previously explained this meaning when commenting on His words ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it." Say, "If I had invented it, you would not be able to avail me anything against God"﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 8]. It is in its apparent sense, and it is by way of supposition (iftirad, hypothetical assumption) with respect to the Prophet ﷺ.

Abu Hayyan considered it unlikely that the pronoun in (taqawwala) refers to the Prophet ﷺ, because such an act is impossible for him ﷺ.

He said: It has been recited in the passive voice with the nominative (bad'in) [i.e., "some" as subject]. He also said: According to the recitation of the majority, the subject of (taqawwala) is implied, its estimated form being: "And if someone fabricated against Us..." Both al-Qurtubi and al-Kashshaf mention this recitation, but Ibn Kathir, al-Tabari, and al-Nisaburi, who are concerned with the recitations, do not mention it. This makes its authenticity doubtful. Yet if it were authentic, it would be admissible. However, what Abu Hayyan deemed unlikely and rejected with respect to the Prophet ﷺ is in fact correct. But it is by way of supposition, so it is not forbidden. Supposition has occurred in the Qur'an in matters greater than this,

as in His words ﴿Say, "If the Most Merciful had a son, I would be the first of the worshippers"﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 81], and His words ﴿Had there been in them (the heavens and the earth) gods other than God, they would have been ruined﴾ [al-Anbiya: 22].

The explicit text on this subject is what the Shaykh said in His words ﴿Say, "If I had invented it, you would not be able to avail me anything against God"﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 8].

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And indeed, it is the truth of certainty.﴾ ﴿So glorify the name of your Lord, the Mighty.﴾

In this is the negation of every falsehood: of poetry, of soothsaying, or of anything else, and of every deficiency or addition.

It has already passed, at the end of Surat al-Waqi'ah, for the Shaykh (may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him) to explain the idafah (construct phrase) of "truth" to "certainty" (haqq al-yaqin), and the meaning of glorifying the name of your Lord (tasbih, the declaration of Allah's transcendence). Haqq al-yaqin is the furthest point of knowledge, since certainty (yaqin) has three levels:

The first: ʿilm al-yaqin (knowledge of certainty).

The second: ʿayn al-yaqin (the eye of certainty).

The third: haqq al-yaqin (the truth of certainty), as in Surat al-Takathur: ﴿Nay, if you knew with the knowledge of certainty﴾ ﴿you would surely see the Hellfire﴾ ﴿Then you would surely see it with the eye of certainty﴾ [al-Takathur: 5–7]. These are two levels, and the third is when they enter it, which is haqq al-yaqin. Its parallel in this world is knowing that the Ka'bah exists and facing it in prayer, then seeing it, which is ʿayn al-yaqin, and then, by entering into it, it becomes haqq al-yaqin. Just as we glorify Allah, meaning we declare Him free of imperfection, so too we declare His speech free of imperfection, because it is one of His attributes.
